data.title: Tree
data.tagline: Expand and browse data with parent-child levels
data.description: A tree reveals folders, departments, categories, and other hierarchies by expanding and collapsing levels. It may support browsing, selection, or dragging. For permissions and selection, explain clearly how parent and child nodes affect each other.

use: Any data with meaningful parent-child levels
avoid: Turn a simple flat list into a tree
Open a very large tree without search or lazy loading
Hide the current selection when branches collapse

lessonPractice.title: A project browser shows folders, nested folders, and files. Users mainly browse location by level and do not submit a selection. How should it be organized?

options.label: Use an expandable tree with parent-child indentation and persistent expansion state
options.feedback: Files naturally form a multi-level hierarchy, and a tree supports gradual browsing while preserving location.

options.label: Put every file and folder in one list sorted only by name
options.feedback: Flattening removes directory membership, making duplicate names and deep locations difficult to understand.

options.label: Choose one path in a cascader and submit before its contents can be viewed
options.feedback: A cascader fits selecting one path. This task needs persistent expansion and sibling comparison rather than submission.

data.agentPrompt: Build the project browser as a tree: folders expand and collapse, files do not, indentation and icons expose levels, and expansion state persists. Test deep nesting, duplicate names, keyboard navigation, and narrow-screen indentation.
